correctness.rationale: The exact Finding is correct. Averaging a polynomial representative against a coordinate-reflection character gives a representative of that parity even when the measure introduces polynomial relations. The sign multiplier can couple S and T only if S symmetric-difference T is the distinguished 2q-set. Below degree q this is impossible; at q it forces complementary one-dimensional squarefree spaces, nonzero by the sphere moments and E[R^(2q)]>0. Both bilinear moments have the same radial factor. The angular numerator is the moment of 2q absolute normal coordinates divided by the radial Gaussian moment; the denominator is the angular moment of q squared coordinates with that same Gaussian radial divisor. Their ratio is (E|N(0,1)|)^(2q)=(2/pi)^q. Each pair gives an off-diagonal centered sign block, with the affine conversion to restriction energy yielding the asserted eigenvalues and squared condition ratio. The monomials are harmonic, giving the pure-band compression as well. The formula for the central multiplicity is correct; the wording 'may be zero' applies to the pure harmonic variant (q=1,d=2), not to the full polynomial band, where constants alone force at least one central eigenvector.
